question.text: An Indian sponsor wants to raise a Cat III fund with (a) mostly US-based HNIs, (b) a few domestic family offices, (c) a long-short India equity strategy, (d) daily NAV. Which structure is OPTIMAL?

answer.text: Pure onshore AIF only; US HNIs subscribe directly via FPI route into the AIF (unified structure)
Pure offshore fund domiciled in Delaware with no India pooling
Master-feeder: onshore AIF master in India + offshore feeder (GIFT-IFSC or Mauritius) for US HNIs + direct domestic subscription channel
Parallel structure with mirror portfolios — not recommended for long-short strategies

explanation.text: The Logic: Master-feeder is optimal: US HNIs subscribe to the feeder (GIFT-IFSC or Mauritius, addressing their home-country tax/regulatory considerations), which feeds the Indian master; domestic investors subscribe directly to the master. Management fee charged at master only (nominal at feeder). One strategy, one portfolio, fair NAV. The Trap: Option A is viable but unified structure can be tax-inefficient for offshore US investors. Option B abandons the Indian sponsor's preference for a domestic manager structure. Option D's parallel has duplicate-fee issues and is commonly less efficient. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D/A/B all touch this decision matrix. XIX-E goes deeper for Cat III. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a GIFT-IFSC feeder, you also capture Section 80LA tax holiday on IFSC-level income — material saving vs. a Mauritius feeder. Model both scenarios before picking.
